liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Comes A Time** (5 reviews): Reviewer thought Comes A Time was long overdue, recognising it from its first notes; Reviewer says the fileset is worth hearing for Comes A Time alone [17][19][20][24][25]
- **Hell in a Bucket** (1 other source): Soundboard levels were low for over half the song and were adjusted; the audience tape also started quietly [5]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Peggy-O and Cassidy stood out in a nine-song first set [25]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): Casey Jones was the reviewer's highlight of the show [25]
- **Days Between** (1 review): Reviewer says the sound is a hi-hat and recalls Billy playing it rather heavily that night [26]
- **I Fought the Law** (1 review): Reviewer found the encore disappointing [24]

## The recordings

- **gd93-03-27.sbd.nawrocki.31956.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 182 min; rated 4.04/5 by 23 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds right on; Soundboard fileset is very crisp, and even Corrina sounds good; Soundboard has clipping or digital noise during Days Between, which reviewer says is not hi-hat [17][19][21][27][28]
- **gd93-03-27.ams-young.georges.6701.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 156 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer prefers the audience recording for its energy, though the board sounds sweet [20]
- **gd1993-03-27.sbd.samaritano-miller.92523.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 155 min; rated 3.29/5 by 7 [4]
- **gd1993-03-27.152952.mtx.seamons.ht133.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 154 min [5]. Said about its sound: Lamarre's tape adds deep bass missing from the soundboard; the arena rumbles, especially during Estimated Prophet [5]

## Around the show

- The Knick crowd had huge energy and sang along on Loose Lucy and Casey Jones [20]
- Reviewer says the Albany arena was one of their favorite places to see the Dead [27]
- Reviewer remembers solid playing throughout and ranks it among the better shows of that year [17]
- Reviewer offers the Eyes>Estimated>Comes A Time run as evidence for doubters of the post-Brent and Bruce era [23]
- Reviewer calls it a best bet for a good 1993 show [24]
- Reviewer calls it one of the best shows of the modern Dead era [26]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd93-03-27.sbd.nawrocki.31956.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> DAT [1]. Also: Soundboard to DAT via D. DiProsa; D. Nawrocki transferred it from D8 through digital coax and a Montego II interface to CD WAV [1]
- **gd93-03-27.ams-young.georges.6701.sbeok.shnf**: taped by James Young; transferred by Nick Georges; source: Audience: Soundfield ST-250's [3]
- **gd1993-03-27.sbd.samaritano-miller.92523.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Samaritano; source: Set 1: SBD -> Dat -> Cassette Master -> Dat ; Set 2: SBD -> Dat [4]. Also: Clean transfer directly from the DATs [4]
- **gd1993-03-27.152952.mtx.seamons.ht133.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro for set 1 and Soundtrack Pro for set 2 (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > Soundtrack > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity >… [5]. Also: Matrix of soundboard and Lamarre's audience tape; first-set soundboard ran slightly fast and was pitch corrected [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by D.King Gallery: [Grateful Dead 3/27/1993 Albany NY Backstage Pass](https://www.dking-gallery.com/store/Dead_Pass_930327.html) [30]
